guideline_source: Wells Criteria + PERC Rule + ESC Guidelines
description: Combined use of PERC Rule (to rule out PE in low-risk patients) and Wells Criteria (to stratify PE probability) for evaluating suspected pulmonary embolism.

inclusion: Adults with symptoms suggestive of PE

decision_rules.description: PE with shock or persistent hypotension

criteria.name: Hypotension
criteria.definition: SBP < 90 mmHg or drop >= 40 mmHg for > 15 minutes

decision_rules.evidence_text: Massive PE with hemodynamic instability has >50% mortality without treatment. Systemic thrombolysis is first-line unless contraindicated.

decision_rules.description: Leg swelling and pain along deep veins
decision_rules.evidence_text: Clinical signs of DVT add 3 points to Wells Score. DVT is source of PE in >90% of cases.

decision_rules.description: PE more likely than alternative diagnosis
decision_rules.evidence_text: When PE is judged more likely than alternative diagnoses, this adds 3 points to Wells Score and often mandates imaging regardless of D-dimer.

action.rationale: Tachycardia adds 1.5 points to Wells Score

decision_rules.evidence_text: Tachycardia (HR > 100) is present in 24-70% of PE patients. Adds 1.5 points to Wells Score.

decision_rules.description: Immobilization >= 3 days or surgery within 4 weeks
decision_rules.evidence_text: Surgery or immobilization within past 4 weeks increases VTE risk 5-10 fold. Adds 1.5 points to Wells Score.
Previous DVT/PE increases recurrence risk 5-8 fold. Adds 1.5 points to Wells Score.
Hemoptysis occurs in 7-30% of PE cases. While nonspecific, it adds 1 point to Wells Score.

decision_rules.description: Cancer treatment within 6 months or palliative
decision_rules.evidence_text: Cancer increases VTE risk 4-7 fold. Active treatment or palliative status adds 1 point to Wells Score.

perc_rule.description: PERC Rule - PE can be ruled out if ALL criteria are NEGATIVE
criteria: No surgery/trauma requiring hospitalization in past 4 weeks
perc_rule.interpretation: If ALL 8 criteria are met and gestalt probability is LOW, PE is effectively ruled out without further testing (false negative rate <2%).

components.criterion: Immobilization >= 3d or surgery in past 4 weeks

interpretation.low: Score <= 4: PE unlikely (8% probability). Check D-dimer, if negative, PE ruled out.
interpretation.high: Score > 4: PE likely (34% probability). Proceed to CTPA.

clarifying_questions.question: Is there any swelling in one leg, especially the calf? Any leg pain?
clarifying_questions.question_zh: 有没有一条腿肿胀，特别是小腿？有没有腿痛？

clarifying_questions.question: Have you had recent surgery, hospitalization, or been bedridden?
clarifying_questions.question_zh: 最近有没有手术、住院或卧床？

clarifying_questions.question: Have you ever had a blood clot in your leg or lung before?
clarifying_questions.question_zh: 以前有没有得过腿部或肺部血栓？

clarifying_questions.question: Have you coughed up any blood?
Are you currently being treated for cancer?
clarifying_questions.question_zh: 您目前在接受癌症治疗吗？

text_chunks.title: Wells Criteria for Pulmonary Embolism
text_chunks.content: The Wells Score stratifies patients into PE Likely or PE Unlikely categories. Score components: Clinical signs of DVT (3 points), PE most likely diagnosis (3 points), Heart rate > 100 (1.5 points), Immobilization/surgery (1.5 points), Previous DVT/PE (1.5 points), Hemoptysis (1 point), Active malignancy (1 point). Score > 4: PE Likely (34% probability, proceed to CTPA). Score <= 4: PE Unlikely (8% probability, check D-dimer).
text_chunks.source: Wells et al, Ann Intern Med 2001

text_chunks.title: PERC Rule for PE Exclusion
text_chunks.content: The PERC Rule can rule out PE without D-dimer testing when pretest probability is LOW and ALL 8 criteria are met: (1) Age < 50, (2) HR < 100, (3) SpO2 >= 95%, (4) No hemoptysis, (5) No estrogen use, (6) No prior DVT/PE, (7) No unilateral leg swelling, (8) No recent surgery/trauma. False negative rate < 2% when properly applied.
text_chunks.source: Kline et al, J Thromb Haemost 2004

text_chunks.title: PE Red Flags - Massive PE Signs
text_chunks.content: Red flags indicating massive or high-risk PE: (1) Hypotension (SBP < 90 or drop >= 40 mmHg), (2) Signs of shock (altered mental status, cool extremities, oliguria), (3) Syncope, (4) Severe dyspnea with cyanosis, (5) RV strain on echo or CT, (6) Elevated troponin or BNP. Massive PE requires consideration of thrombolysis or embolectomy.

text_chunks.title: Pulmonary Embolism Overview
text_chunks.content: Pulmonary embolism occurs when a blood clot, usually from deep leg veins, travels to the pulmonary arteries. Symptoms include: dyspnea (73%), pleuritic chest pain (66%), cough (37%), leg swelling (28%), hemoptysis (13%), syncope (5%). PE is often missed because symptoms are nonspecific and overlap with other conditions. High index of suspicion needed, especially with VTE risk factors.

text_chunks.title: PE Initial Management
text_chunks.content: Initial PE management: (1) Supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 > 90%, (2) IV access, (3) Hemodynamic support with fluids if hypotensive (avoid aggressive fluids - may worsen RV failure), (4) Anticoagulation with LMWH or unfractionated heparin once confirmed/highly suspected, (5) For massive PE: thrombolysis (alteplase 100mg over 2h) or surgical/interventional embolectomy, (6) IVC filter if anticoagulation contraindicated with acute proximal DVT.
